terms.definition: The data total divided by the number of data points — the average.
terms.function: The one-value fair share of the whole dataset.
terms.whereItIs: The level line across the bins.
terms.whyItMatters: The mean is the most quotable number in data.

terms.definition: The value every point would get if all data were shared evenly.
terms.function: Think of pouring all values into one pile and re-dividing.
terms.whereItIs: Each bin leveled to the same height.
terms.whyItMatters: Fair share makes the formula feel true.

terms.definition: The two ingredients of the mean — the total and the number of points.
terms.whereItIs: The plate at the front of the table.
terms.whyItMatters: Forgetting either part breaks the computation.

terms.definition: A very large or small point pulls the mean strongly.
terms.function: Every point is added, so extremes shift the total.
terms.whereItIs: Visible when a huge bin joins the table.
terms.whyItMatters: Outlier sensitivity is why some datasets prefer the median.
